title: Predict string allocation and equality behavior and distinguish UTF-16 code units from user-perceived characters

rubric.point: Strings are immutable: concatenation creates a new string assigned to second, leaving first referring to "reed".
String == compares contents, and "reed" differs from "reeds".

questions.model: Concatenation creates a new string, `"reeds"`, and reassigns `second`; `first` remains `"reed"` because strings are immutable. String `==` compares contents, which now differ.

questions.prompt: A .NET label contains `"a\u0308"`: a base letter followed by a combining diaeresis, displayed together as one user-perceived character. Why does `label.EnumerateRunes().Count()` return 2 rather than 1?
options: Rune enumeration counts UTF-16 code units, so it splits the displayed character into two storage units.
Rune enumeration counts Unicode scalar values, so the letter and combining mark remain separate scalars.
Rune enumeration counts user-perceived characters, so the combining mark becomes a separate displayed character.
Rune enumeration counts encoded UTF-8 bytes, so the letter and combining mark each contribute one byte.

rubric.point: Selects the explanation that the letter and combining mark are separate Unicode scalar values within one user-perceived character.

questions.model: Rune enumeration counts Unicode scalar values, so the letter and combining mark remain separate scalars.

c1.text: The string have overriden equality comparer which compares strings by the values, even they are ref types

annotations.quote: The string have overriden equality comparer which compares strings by the values
annotations.note: You correctly say string `==` compares by value, but you never connect it to the specific values here, "reed" and "reeds", so the second rubric point is not shown.
Noting that strings are reference types with value-based equality is accurate background, but it does not answer why the two variables differ.
You needed to say that strings are immutable, so `+=` creates a new string "reeds" assigned to `second` while `first` still refers to "reed". You also needed to say that the contents now differ.

c1.feedback: You stated that string equality compares values, but you did not explain immutability or that `second` now holds different content from `first`.
